# zrscl

> Multiplies a complex vector by the reciprocal of a complex scalar.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zrscl from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zrscl';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zrscl( N, a, x, strideX ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements |
| `a` | `Complex128` | Complex scalar divisor |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output complex vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `x` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of components of the vector x.
- `a`: The scalar a which is used to divide each component of x. A must not be 0, or the subroutine will divide by zero.
- `x`: The n-element vector x.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: input array

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zrscl.ndarray( N, a, x, strideX, offsetX ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements |
| `a` | `Complex128` | Complex scalar divisor |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output complex vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `x` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of components of the vector x.
- `a`: The scalar a which is used to divide each component of x. A must not be 0, or the subroutine will divide by zero.
- `x`: The n-element vector x.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: input array

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zrscl()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZRSCL`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zrscl.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Complex128 from '@stdlib/complex/float64/ctor/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zrscl from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zrscl';

const x = new Complex128Array( [ 6.0, 8.0, 12.0, 16.0 ] );
const a = new Complex128( 2.0, 0.0 );

zrscl( 2, a, x, 1 );

const view = reinterpret( x, 0 );
console.log( 'Result: [%s]', view.join( ', ' ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => Result: [3, 4, 6, 8]
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZRSCL`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZRSCL multiplies an n-element complex vector x by the complex scalar 1/a. This is done without overflow or underflow as long as the final result x/a does not overflow or underflow.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
